regulations.name: DORA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
regulations.why: Orvanta is a financial entity. Covers ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and ICT third parties.
regulations.verification: Verified: EUR-Lex. Art. 2(1)(b) lists payment institutions; Art. 64 sets application from 17 January 2025.

regulations.name: GDPR, Regulation (EU) 2016/679
regulations.why: Controller for customer and staff data. Baku access is a restricted transfer.
regulations.verification: Azerbaijan absent from the European Commission adequacy list (checked 2026-11-07). [verify against official source]: Inspectorate role; official site not reachable.

regulations.name: Payment services rules (PSD2, Directive (EU) 2015/2366, as transposed)
regulations.why: Basis of the payment institution licence, including safeguarding and strong customer authentication.
regulations.verification: Bank of Lithuania site lists its supervision of payment institutions. [verify against official source]: Lithuanian transposing act references.

regulations.name: AML and counter-terrorist financing rules
regulations.why: Customer due diligence, monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.
regulations.verification: [verify against official source]: competent authority and act references. Context only; outside the portfolio's security scope.

regulations.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
regulations.why: Contractual through the card program. Vault is outsourced, yet card data has appeared in tickets.
regulations.verification: Verified: PCI SSC blog. v4.0.1 published June 2024; v4.0 retired 31 December 2024. Orvanta's validation level requires QSA or scheme confirmation.

regulations.name: NIS2, Directive (EU) 2022/2555, and Lithuanian Law on Cyber Security
regulations.why: Awareness item. DORA takes precedence for matters it covers, but Baku subsidiary and group scope need legal confirmation.
regulations.verification: DORA recital 16 (lex specialis) verified on EUR-Lex. [verify against official source]: Lithuanian transposition dates; secondary sources give 18 October 2024.

regulations.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and Amendment 1:2024
regulations.why: Commercial requirement from enterprise merchants, not a legal duty. The amendment adds a climate-change relevance check to clause 4.
regulations.verification: Amendment content confirmed through a national standards body's published copy and certification-body notes.

observations.fact: Risk register is one spreadsheet, last updated February 2025, with no criteria or owners.
observations.attacker_view: Nobody has asked which path to the ledger is the easiest, so nobody has closed it.

observations.fact: Shared admin accounts remain in the AWS legacy account, Orbit and the DBA credential.
observations.attacker_view: One stolen shared password gives high privilege with no named person in the logs.

observations.fact: Last 18 leavers: median removal 9 days, worst case 37 days.
observations.attacker_view: A former engineer may keep working credentials for weeks.

observations.fact: Okta apps have MFA. Metabase, Jenkins, OpenVPN, Kyrovia and agent Zendesk logins do not enforce it.
observations.attacker_view: Phishing and credential stuffing go straight to the tools Okta does not guard.

observations.fact: Daily backups run, but no full restore is on record. Backups share the production account.
observations.attacker_view: Ransomware operators with account access can delete backups before encrypting data.

observations.fact: 0 of 20 vendors have a documented security assessment. No DORA register is complete.
observations.attacker_view: The weakest supplier with customer data becomes the easiest way in.

observations.fact: CloudTrail is off in 1 of 5 AWS accounts. There is no SIEM and no scheduled log review.
observations.attacker_view: An intruder can stay in the environment because no one is looking.

observations.fact: Draft plan dates from 2023. It has no regulatory timelines and has never been exercised.
observations.attacker_view: Confusion in the first hours gives attackers time to escalate and reporting clocks run.

observations.fact: Branch protection covers 61% of repositories. 14% of Q3 2026 production deployments bypassed review.
observations.attacker_view: A compromised developer account can ship malicious code to production unreviewed.

observations.fact: A March 2026 search found 11 Zendesk tickets containing full card numbers pasted by customers.
observations.attacker_view: A local agent login opens a searchable store of card numbers.

observations.fact: Baku engineers can view production personal data. No documented transfer impact assessment exists.
observations.attacker_view: Broad remote production access widens the blast radius of any stolen laptop session.

observations.fact: The CISO-designate, hired in September 2026, reports to the CTO, whose teams own most gaps.
observations.attacker_view: Risks that slow delivery can be deprioritized before they reach the board.

maturity.basis: Roles exist; no ISMS or board reporting
Terraform, encryption and Multi-AZ in place
